exclusions.title: Desktop multitouch input injection
exclusions.reason: The injector exists and works to the kernel boundary (conformance/desktop-touch.mjs, tools/uinput_touch_device.c): it creates a virtual touchscreen unprivileged, the kernel enumerates it with INPUT_PROP_DIRECT and the four ABS_MT_* axes, and contacts are aimed at the window's real rectangle. Nothing downstream reads it on this host. /dev/input/event* is root:input 0660 and this user is not in the input group, so SDL's evdev path cannot open it; and the lane runs under Xvfb, which has no evdev backend at all. This is a host and display-server constraint, not a missing capability. Evidence: docs/verification/desktop-multitouch-2026-08-15-r2.md.

colour grade table and film grain
tests.reason: A known 17^3 .cube uploaded as a Data3DTexture and sampled by lut3D, with the film grain node at zero intensity, on the host as well as the browser. The grade and grain stages are generated template source, so a host that cannot carry a 3D texture upload and a trilinear filter leaves a game broken where it ships. The table is deliberately not the identity, so a host that ignored the upload or substituted a constant fails it; the parsed texture is read back in JS against the table's own formula, and the frame is compared to the browser reference within the row's tolerance. Tolerance 0.04, measured on PR 473 (hosted llvmpipe vs Chrome): 2.4% of pixels differ, 0.04% by more than 2 levels, mean deltaE 0.047; the rest is 1-2 level rounding in the 3D table filter.

terrain merge and seam jobs settle inline on a workerless host
tests.reason: The block merge and the seam bridge strip move off the main thread where a worker exists; a host with no worker runs the same functions inline. The scene hides Worker for the settle, hashes every settled block and bridge by raw position/normal/index bytes, and requires the fingerprint to equal the node inline path's pinned constant. A host that dropped, reordered or approximated the inline result fails on the hash before the frame is compared, and the frame is compared to the browser reference within the row's tolerance. Tolerance 0.06, measured on PR 473 (hosted llvmpipe vs Chrome): 4.6% of pixels differ, 0.04% by more than 2 levels, mean deltaE 0.034; the rest is 1-2 level shading rounding.

generatedPlaytestProofs.title: generated shooter relative look, right-button aim, left-button fire, aimed shot on the crosshair
generatedPlaytestProofs.runner: packages/playtest CLI --target desktop|android against the scaffolded project
generatedPlaytestProofs.reason: This proof drives a scaffolded generated game, not a conformance scene: registry tests[] rows are executed by the visual-parity lanes and must export startScene scenes, so a playtest scenario cannot live there without breaking those lanes. It is registered here so the versioned public registry still records it; the owning runner executes it on web and desktop, and an unreachable device lane is reported blocked, never passed.

generatedPlaytestProofs.title: generated starter composed render chain: sharpen and bloom report their tier
generatedPlaytestProofs.runner: packages/playtest CLI --target desktop and --target android against the scaffolded starter project
generatedPlaytestProofs.reason: This proof drives the generated starter's real renderer through one scenario with two ordered stages, then requires a non-blank native screenshot and the TN_RENDER_CHAIN high-tier marker. The desktop and Android commands are the same scenario contract; a missing device or runtime is reported blocked by the runner, never converted into a pass.

generatedPlaytestProofs.title: native physics collision events: started/stopped parity with the web EventQueue path, no per-step pair polling
generatedPlaytestProofs.runner: packages/runtime-native package.json native:physics:parity (cargo test --lib on the host toolchain); red-green tests live in native/physics/src/lib.rs
generatedPlaytestProofs.reason: The native host synthesized collision events by polling every body pair every step (O(n^2) narrow-phase graph lookups; measured 25.7x step-cost growth from 16 to 128 bodies and ~0.2 ms/frame on the PRD-227-P2 device profile). The step now drains Rapier's own collision transitions through an EventHandler, the same event source the web path reads (packages/physics/src/simulation.ts drainCollisionEvents). The Rust tests assert the [leftId, rightId, started, 1] record contract the TypeScript consumer reads (packages/physics/src/plugin.ts), started-once/stopped-once delivery, sensor overlap parity, removal dropping unknown-collider events exactly like the web byCollider filter, and a scaling bound (8x bodies must not multiply per-step cost by more than 20x; measured 4.3x after the fix).

generatedPlaytestProofs.title: native physics character feet-on-floor parity with the real CharacterBody3D subject
generatedPlaytestProofs.runner: packages/runtime-native package.json native:physics:parity (web measurement plus cargo test --test parity against the Rust Simulation backend)
generatedPlaytestProofs.reason: The web arm executes the public CharacterBody3D, CollisionShape3D, RigidBody3D, and Rapier plugin lifecycle in the collected parity artifact; the Rust arm runs the shipping native Simulation with the same floor, capsule, gravity, offset, and 30 fixed steps. The parity test requires exact grounded and ground-collider agreement plus bounded ground-normal and resting-position deltas, so a native floor perturbation cannot leave a green web-only JSON proof.
